---
title: "Tutorial"
---

Earth2Studio.jl re-exports the `earth2studio` Python module and its submodules as `Py` objects. Anything you can do in Python you can do in Julia by calling into these objects via [PythonCall.jl](https://github.com/JuliaPy/PythonCall.jl).

## Exposed names

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using Earth2Studio

earth2studio  # earth2studio
data          # earth2studio.data
models        # earth2studio.models  (use models.px and models.dx)
perturbation  # earth2studio.perturbation
io            # earth2studio.io
run           # earth2studio.run
statistics    # earth2studio.statistics
utils         # earth2studio.utils
```

Each is a `PythonCall.Py` reference — attribute access, calls, and conversions work the way they do in PythonCall.

## Auto-conversion of common Julia types

PythonCall handles the conversions you most often need at call sites:

| Julia               | Python                          |
|---------------------|---------------------------------|
| `DateTime`          | `datetime.datetime`             |
| `Vector{DateTime}`  | `list[datetime.datetime]`       |
| `String`            | `str`                           |
| `Vector{String}`    | `list[str]`                     |

So you can pass these directly:

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using Earth2Studio
using Dates

ds = data.ARCO()
da = ds(DateTime(2023, 6, 15), ["t2m", "u10m"])             # one time
da = ds([DateTime(2023, 6, 15), DateTime(2023, 6, 16)], "t2m")  # several
```

Two practical caveats:

- `Date` (no time component) is converted to Python's `datetime.date`, which earth2studio mixes with `datetime.datetime` internally and triggers `TypeError`. Wrap with `DateTime(d)` first.
- If a Python API specifically wants a `numpy.datetime64` array (some lower-level entry points do), build it explicitly: `pyimport("numpy").array([pyimport("numpy").datetime64("2023-06-15T00:00:00")])`.

## Fetching data

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using Earth2Studio
using PythonCall: pyconvert, PyArray
using Dates

ds = data.ARCO()
da = ds(DateTime(2023, 6, 15), ["t2m", "u10m"])

pyconvert(Tuple, da.dims)        # ("time", "variable", "lat", "lon")
pyconvert(Tuple, da.shape)       # (1, 2, 721, 1440)

arr = PyArray(da.values)         # zero-copy PyArray{Float64, 4}
t2m = arr[1, 1, :, :]            # 721 × 1440 lat × lon Kelvin
```

## Prognostic models

```{julia}
#| eval: false
pkg   = models.px.FCN.load_default_package()
model = models.px.FCN.load_model(pkg)
model.to("cuda")
```

## Diagnostic models

```{julia}
#| eval: false
pkg = models.dx.PrecipitationAFNO.load_default_package()
dx  = models.dx.PrecipitationAFNO.load_model(pkg)
```

## Workflows

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using Dates

backend = io.ZarrBackend("/tmp/forecast.zarr")

# Deterministic
run.deterministic([DateTime(2023, 6, 15)], 10, model, ds, backend)

# Ensemble
perturb = perturbation.SphericalGaussian()
run.ensemble([DateTime(2023, 6, 15)], 10, 4, model, ds, backend, perturb; batch_size=4)

# Diagnostic
run.diagnostic([DateTime(2023, 6, 15)], 10, model, dx, ds, backend)
```

## IO backends

```{julia}
#| eval: false
io.ZarrBackend("/tmp/out.zarr")
io.NetCDF4Backend("/tmp/out.nc")
io.AsyncZarrBackend("/tmp/out.zarr")
io.XarrayBackend()
io.KVBackend()
```

## Statistics

```{julia}
#| eval: false
m = statistics.rmse(reduction_dimensions=["time"])
m = statistics.acc(reduction_dimensions=["time"])
m = statistics.crps(ensemble_dimension="ensemble")
```

## Bringing results back to Julia

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using PythonCall

# numpy / xarray array → Julia
a_jl   = pyconvert(Array, da.values)   # copies
a_view = PyArray(da.values)            # zero-copy view
```

Refer to the [PythonCall.jl docs](https://juliapy.github.io/PythonCall.jl/stable/) for more conversion utilities, and to the [earth2studio docs](https://nvidia.github.io/earth2studio/) for the Python API itself.
